# TurnOver 1.0, build 13
### New to try - Your own tester key: the first time this build starts, TurnOver asks for the personal key in your email from Oliver. Open the link in that email, or paste the key into the box. Each beta build now works for 90 days, and every update starts that again. TurnOver menu, Tester key says whose key it is and until when this build works. - Hints, as in VoiceOver: pause on an item and TurnOver says what you can do with it ("Space presses it", "Return opens its page"), with hints of their own in Mail, Safari, Terminal, Word, Finder, Claude, TextEdit and the App Store. Turn them off in the TurnOver menu, Preferences, Presentation, Hints. - The App Store (preview, off until you turn it on in the TurnOver menu, Applications). Up and Down go through every app on the page, the whole of each shelf rather than three at a time; Left and Right jump between shelves, saying each one's name and size. Return opens an app's page, which reads in order: the app and its price, its rating, age rating, chart place, developer and size, the description, reviews, What's New, privacy, the developer's accessibility notes and more. Space presses the app's button (Open, Get, Update, Re-download), and so does Return on the app's own page; a price needs two presses, so nothing is bought by accident. Tab moves to the sidebar (Search, Discover, Arcade, Updates…); Command F searches and reads the results; Escape goes back. - Quick keys wrap round the page: after the last heading, H goes on from the top and says "wrapped to the top" (Shift H: "wrapped to the bottom"). Turn it off in the TurnOver menu, Preferences, Browse mode. - VoiceOver's way of moving, in the Mac style: VO Left and Right move within a group (a toolbar, a sidebar, a list, a pane) in the order things are on screen, and stop at its end; a group says how many items it holds ("tool bar, 9 items"), VO Shift Down goes into it and VO Shift Up comes back out. Tab and the arrows are unchanged. Turn it off in the TurnOver menu, Preferences, Keyboard. - TurnOver Left and Right now move through everything in the window, item by item, going in and out of groups by themselves, as Narrator's Caps Lock arrows do. Handy in alerts and dialogs where Tab misses things. TurnOver Shift with the arrows still works as before. The current word is TurnOver W, and the current sentence TurnOver Control S. - Mail: Escape leaves the message you're reading, as in Outlook on Windows: a message in its own window closes, and you're back in the message list. - Music, Podcasts and TV (previews, off until you turn them on in the TurnOver menu, Applications). Up and Down now go through the whole page, every shelf and every item on it, reading further down as you go; End goes to the very last item. Left and Right jump between shelves, Tab moves between the sidebar, the page and the player, Return opens or plays, and Escape goes back, landing on the item you opened. A video from Music's Radio page plays in its own player; Space plays and pauses, Escape leaves it.
### Fixed - Braille tables in every language macOS has, not only your Mac's own: TurnOver menu, Preferences, Braille, Braille table, Other languages (Slovenian, Italian, Arabic and many more). (reported by a tester) - Finder's sidebar: move TurnOver's cursor into it (TurnOver Right in the Windows style, VO Shift Down in the Mac style), then Up and Down go through it, Return or Space opens that place, and Left and Right close and open its sections; Escape goes back. Finder never gives its sidebar the keyboard, so TurnOver works it for you. Tab and Shift Tab go round the window as in Windows Explorer: files, sidebar, toolbar, search, and back to the files. Elsewhere, when the cursor lands on something that can take the keyboard, the keyboard now goes there too, as in VoiceOver and Narrator. The toolbar's Back and Forward and its four view buttons are now items of their own. - More of VoiceOver's keys in the Mac style: VO Home and End (first and last item), VO Command Home and End (top and bottom of the window), VO Up and Down, VO Shift Escape, VO J (jump to the linked item), VO Return (select), VO Backslash (disclosure triangle), VO Shift Space (click), VO Shift H (help tag), VO Shift N (hint), VO Shift W (read the window), VO Shift U (link address), VO Command Space (actions) and VO F2 twice (window chooser). - The list of shortcuts (TurnOver Slash) shows the keys for the style you're using: in the Windows style, the VoiceOver keys were hiding some Windows ones. - Return on a button you've tabbed to in an alert now presses that button. macOS sends Return to the alert's default button whatever has the focus, so "Open System Settings" could press "Deny". - Claude: a summary line that stayed the same ("Ran 23 commands, compacted the session…") was read again every few seconds while Claude worked. A name is now read only when it changes. - Hints are only spoken for where you still are: a hint for the message list was said as a message window came up. - Mail: quoted text says its level as you read into it ("quote level 1", "quote level 2"), as VoiceOver does; and a message opened in its own window (with the preview pane hidden) starts reading in the message, not on the toolbar (reported by a tester). - Pages in two languages: TurnOver's own words ("link", "heading") are said by your main voice, not the other language's; text in another script is read by that language's voice even when the page doesn't say which language it is; and each language can have its own speech rate (TurnOver menu, Preferences, Speech, the language, Rate) (reported by a tester). - Hints are no longer spoken over a page being read out, and edit fields no longer get the obvious "Type to enter text". - Typing: after deleting a letter, the word is said as it now is ("think", Backspace, Space says "thin"), and Option Backspace says "deleted" and the word (reported by a tester). - Brave, Chrome and Edge: H and Shift H move through every heading both ways; Shift H said "no previous heading", and H could skip one (reported by a tester). - Selecting a paragraph on a web page or in a message (Shift Option Up and Down) is read, as character, word and line selection are (reported by a tester). - New to try: each thing to try opens into a list of its lines, to arrow through, instead of one long item (reported by a tester). - In a one-line field (a search box, the To field), Up and Down read the field instead of only playing the edge sound (reported by a tester). - "New line" on Return can be turned off: TurnOver menu, Preferences, Keyboard, Say new line on Return (reported by a tester). - Reading quickly with the arrows no longer plays the edge sound in the middle of text (reported by a tester). - Touch ID and password prompts (such as the App Store confirming your Apple Account) now say their message first, then their button, instead of "coreautha, Untitled, window". - Dialogs that are more like pages (the App Store's account window) are read line by line with Up and Down, text as well as buttons; a web page inside a dialog is read in browse mode.

# TurnOver 1.0, build 12
### New to try - Screen recognition (OCR), as NVDA's TurnOver R: TurnOver reads the text in the window from the screen, for apps that don't tell a screen reader what's in them (games, Steam, pictures of text). Press TurnOver R where TurnOver leads, or Command Control R anywhere, even where VoiceOver leads. Up and Down move through rows; Left and Right by character, with Option or Control by word; Tab jumps between columns and sections; Return or Space clicks the word you're on, Shift Return right-clicks, Option Return double-clicks; M moves the mouse there without clicking; TurnOver R again re-reads; Escape closes. Columns, like a sidebar beside the main text, are read one after the other, and lists and tables row by row. It works on a braille display too: routing keys move to a word, and pressed again click it. The first time, macOS asks for Screen Recording permission for TurnOver. Options are in Preferences, Screen recognition. - Application chooser: every app with a window, including system alerts that Command Tab leaves out (such as macOS asking to allow Screen Recording), with each app's windows under it. Return switches there. Mac style: TurnOver F1 twice, as in VoiceOver. Windows style: Option Tab, as Windows+Tab is Task View.
### Fixed - Safari: after reloading a page, the arrows could say "nothing on this page yet" while the page was there (Tab reached it). Safari had swapped the page for a new one; TurnOver now moves to it. - Context menus say "context menu" as they open, from VO Shift M, the right Option key or Shift F10.

# TurnOver 1.0, build 11
### New to try - Keyboard style: Mac, which works like VoiceOver key for key (as now), or Windows, which makes the Mac feel like a PC with NVDA: NVDA's commands on the TurnOver key, Command alone for the menus, Option alone for the Dock, F1 to F12 as function keys, and in Finder, Return opens and F2 renames. Switch with TurnOver Shift K, or Keyboard style in the TurnOver menu. More Windows keys are on the way. - Windows keys for editing, in the Windows style: Control C, X, V, A, Z, S, O, N, P, F and W do what Command does with them; Control Y redoes; Home and End go to the start and end of the line, Control Home and Control End to the start and end of the document; Control with the arrows moves by word or paragraph; Control Backspace deletes a word; Command F4 quits an app (Alt F4). Terminal keeps its own Control keys. These apply where TurnOver leads; where VoiceOver leads, the keys are the Mac's as always. - Input help: press Escape twice to leave it. - Unverified apps: in the TurnOver menu, Applications, Unverified apps lists every app you have open that TurnOver hasn't been checked with yet. Switch any of them to TurnOver to try it; they may not read well, and feedback on them is welcome.
### Fixed - The Dock: after Escape, TurnOver kept reading the Dock with nothing selected and the arrows went back into it. Escape now returns to the app you were in, and the arrows in the Dock are the Dock's own (Left and Right move, Up opens the item's menu). - Safari: when a page stopped answering for a few seconds, TurnOver could be left with nothing to read until you switched apps. It now looks again once Safari answers, and treats a page with no address yet as still loading.
